To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
particle filters are asymptotically exact and asymptotically optimal.

(i) the bootstrap particle filtering method is optimal in the sense that the variance of the filtering error is minimal among a large class of sequential Monte Carlo methods, and (ii) the particle smoothing algorithm is optimal in the same sense as the bootstrap filter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel algorithms and techniques for sequential Bayesian estimation, and their application in fields as diverse computer vision, econometric and navigation.
the design of algorithms to solve optimal filtering, smoothing and prediction problems for non linear, non Gaussian state space processes.
the design of algorithms for the solution of the optimal estimation problem for nonlinear, non Gaussian dynamic systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
particle methods are a powerful and flexible tool to solve optimal estimation problems for non-linear non-Gaussian models in an online fashion.

particle filtering and smoothing methods are now well established and have become a standard tool for the numerical solution of a wide range of estimation problems, in a large variety of applications.

the field of sequential Monte Carlo methods for state space models has now reached a state of maturity, where the basic ideas are well established, and the main algorithms are now well known and understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided a tutorial on particle filtering and smoothing, and have done so in a manner that should be accessible to a broad audience.
the field is still evolving, with a number of interesting and important open research problems.
we have developed a complete theory for particle methods for filtering and smoothing in the context of non linear non Gaussian models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the particle filtering literature is much richer than is generally perceived.

particle methods can be understood in a unified way using a general framework that encompasses all particle methods, and that this general framework can be used to derive new particle methods, as well as to understand existing ones.
particle filtering and smoothing are now well established as a class of methods to solve a large class of estimation problems.
